newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu faces sleaze charges.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu faces sleaze charges.

text.p: Police said on Wednesday Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal.
The news, broken by Israeli television stations, dealt a crippling although not necessarily fatal political blow to the right-wing leader, analysts said.
It came during a visit by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross who is trying to salvage Israeli-Palestinian peace talks. Both Ross and Palestinian officials called the news an internal Israeli affair.
Israel's state prosecutor can choose to ignore the police recommendation to put Netanyahu on trial for his short-lived appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general.
But a minister close to Netanyahu said the Likud party leader might have to call an election if the present attorney general decided to prosecute.
Police Chief Assaf Hefetz told reporters the recommendation against Netanyahu was "softer" than that against three others in the so-called Bar-On-for-Hebron scandal.
"But in principle the text is that there is evidence for bringing an indictment against the prime minister on the charge of fraud and breach of trust."
Netanyahu's lawyer said the charges were "baseless".

Asked what Netanyahu wanted to do about the police recommendation, his attorney Yaacov Weinroth told Israel's Channel One television: "Contact the prosecution to try to convince the prosecution that it is baseless."

The attorney confirmed police had recommended charging Netanyahu with breach of trust. But Weinroth said prosecutors told him that the recommendation came with reservations that raised doubts about its strength.

"If what I have been told is correct -- and I imagine what I was told by the prosecution was correct -- this recommendation says that even if it is accepted, it is subject to a summary interrogation of the prime minister," he said.

Channel One television said police had urged in a 995-page report to the state prosecution on Tuesday that Netanyahu be charged with fraud and breach of trust in the appointment of Bar-On. It said police had also recommended three figures close to Netanyahu be put on trial.
Asked what would happen if prosecutors pressed charges, Health Minister Yehoshua Matza, who is close to Netanyahyu, told Israel Radio in English: "Perhaps it will be to go back to elections."
Netanyahu was elected with a slim 30,000 vote-majority over Labour's Shimon Peres last May.
Matza said there would be no other option since under a law first applied in last May's ballot, the prime minister is chosen directly in a poll separate from parliamentary elections.
Matza said that even with the police recommendation, Netanyahu's centre-right coalition government can stay in office.
"Of course it can go on because it's only a recommendation. The final decision will be taken by the attorney general and we have to wait for his decision," Matza said.
Asked if the prime minister should resign, Matza said: "No. We are a state of law. And we have to wait as I have said for the resolution, for the decision of the attorney general."
Peres said if the recommendation were true, it would be "a political earthquake" and warrant calling early elections.

Police have been looking into the Bar-On appointment since January. At the time Channel One alleged that a Netanyahu ally on trial for corruption, politician Aryeh Deri, had pushed Bar-On for the job in the hope of winning a plea bargain. Deri had promised his Shas party's support for Netanyahu's deal with the Palestinians to redeploy in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Bar-On himself quit hours after being appointed amid criticism he was professionally unfit for the job. The case has dominated the Israeli press during the 12 weeks of police investigation,

"In any event I have no doubt, no doubt whatsoever, that the prime minister has no problem with this affair -- that he will emerge completely clean from this matter," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said.
